trajectory.patch:
Based on the analysis of the error log and source code, the test failure is due to a race condition. The `k_yield()` call in `drive_reset_on_wait()` does not guarantee that the `treceiver` thread has reached the `k_event_wait_all()` call before the main test thread proceeds to post new events.

If the main thread posts events before the receiver thread calls `k_event_wait_all()` with the `reset` flag, those newly posted events will be cleared by the `reset` operation, leading to an incorrect state in the event object when the assertion is checked.

Replacing `k_yield()` with `k_sleep(DELAY)` ensures that the `treceiver` thread has sufficient time to execute and pend on the event wait, clearing the old events and preparing to receive new ones. This is consistent with the synchronization method used in subsequent parts of the same test function.

Here is the fix:

tests/kernel/events/event_api/src/main.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
	k_sem_give(&sync_sem);
	k_yield();           /* Give receiver thread time to run */
	k_event_post(&test_event, 0x123);
========
	k_sem_give(&sync_sem);
	k_sleep(DELAY);      /* Give receiver thread time to run */
	k_event_post(&test_event, 0x123);
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
